_readme: Q89 inc.13 — the FIRST scorer bundle built from a meeting already published to prod.
WHAT THIS FILE IS. `meeting-next-steps` (~/.claude/skills/meeting-next-steps) ranks next steps;
`lib/meetings/nextStepsAdapter.ts` (inc.12) carries its ranks into the four-block surface. Until
now nothing had ever fed the scorer real data, so the adapter was tested only against fixtures
this repo invented. This bundle is the real input: every field below comes out of the already-
archived deep read at
`MLE Internal Meetings/archive-reads/2026-06-16-gulfcoast-ai-alex-one.deepread.txt`,
the same file that produced `2026-06-16-gulfcoast-ai-alex-one.activity.json` in inc.11.
NOTHING NEW WAS MINED. The four actions are the four `to_do` blocks; the pains, talking points
and benefits are the same entries already live on C-2018. This increment re-expresses what is
on the record in the scorer's schema — it does not re-read the meeting, and it must not add a
fact the published activity does not already carry.
SOURCE LINES ARE LITERAL. The scorer's gate A rejects any `source_line` that is not a substring
of the --transcript file, so where an activity `excerpt` was elided with `…` (the summary-bullet
entries) the bundle carries a shorter span that IS literal. All 14 were grep-verified against
the deep read before this file was written.
OWNERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED ON PURPOSE. The Notion body lists four to_dos and never says who owns
one. Reading `us` onto them because they sound like our prep is exactly the inference inc.11
refused when it wrote all four `open` rather than guessing them done. `UNRESOLVED` is the
record's answer; the scorer surfaces it in its own block (gate F) instead of hiding it.
STATUS IS STILL NOT INFERRED. A1 says 'before tomorrow's meeting' and that meeting happened
seven weeks ago; A1 will therefore score as badly aged. That is the record talking, not a claim
the work is outstanding — the page never says it was done, and 'very likely done' is not a
status.
EVIDENCE IS A QUOTE OR IT IS NULL. The scorer checks every `evidence` value against the
transcript too — reasoning parked there gets refused as a fabricated source line, and it is
right to: `evidence` is what the rung rests on, `rationale` is why we read it that way. This
bundle was refused once for exactly that and rewritten. Most rungs here have NO quote behind
them, because a to_do list does not say who is waiting or how long a job takes — those are
null with the reasoning in `rationale`, never a sentence dressed up as a line from the call.

items.title: Price Bold Trail for the Boomtown comparison
items.source_line: Look into Bold Trail pricing for comparison

rationale.access_unlocked: Public pricing lookup — no human on the other side.
rationale.deal_value: No figure, and no monetized path: the record says the Boomtown decision is already made against migration.

pain_points.quote: Google is moving towards zero-click listings, meaning when people search, you know, people's homes for sale, it comes up right in the Google AI overview so they don't go to our site anymore
pain_points.speaker: UNRESOLVED (Gulf Coast principal)
pain_points.maps_to: The organic/attribution gap the SEO teardown (A1) opened
pain_points.attribution_note: The deep read is an unattributed transcript. The side is established by the paragraph being the answer to a question Rob asked, not by speaker tagging.

pain_points.quote: I know it's just like hard to quantify organic for 60 agents. You know what I mean? Like, how do I, I don't know how to present that to them.
pain_points.speaker: UNRESOLVED (Gulf Coast principal)
pain_points.maps_to: Attribution reporting - the deliverable he says he cannot produce himself
pain_points.attribution_note: Same unattributed transcript; established as his by being the answer to Rob's question in the preceding paragraph.

pain_points.quote: that is where we're weak, right? 'Cause we became so headstrong on PPC and developing the agents to learn how to convert PPC into clients. That's been our main pain point that we try to consistently solve is how to take these internet lookers and turn them into clients.
pain_points.speaker: UNRESOLVED (Gulf Coast principal)
pain_points.maps_to: Conversion, not traffic - what any site we hand him is judged on

pain_points.quote: The worst part about Boomtown is they're very... with their API. Native API. They don't play well with others. So I'm having to do all these workarounds to improve the technology of it.
pain_points.speaker: UNRESOLVED (Gulf Coast principal)
pain_points.maps_to: Why he is building a replacement he owns outright rather than migrating

talking_points.point: He is not shopping for a website - he is diversifying off PPC and building four products at once (HyperLocal website factory, HomeCloneVault, a solopreneur home-services utility, an internal app for 60 agents). Anything we propose should attach to one of those four, not sit beside them.
talking_points.why: Attaching to a product he has already funded is a different conversation from selling him a fifth thing.

talking_points.point: HyperLocal has a date and a price he has already thought about: go-to-market October/November at roughly $699-899/month as a pure licence. He explicitly prefers a higher fixed fee over a revenue share because he does not want to rely on other people's talent to get paid.
talking_points.why: His own pricing instinct, in his own numbers - quote against it, not over it.
talking_points.source_line: I'd rather go with a higher monthly fee because I don't want to rely on talent.

talking_points.point: The Boomtown decision is already made and it is a two-year one: stay on legacy Boomtown for the ad-buying power, migrate nothing, and build the replacement he owns. Pitching a migration is pitching against a decision.
talking_points.why: Agents tested Bold Trail and rejected it; moving 60 of them is impractical.

talking_points.point: On HomeCloneVault he already has money out the door and a partner circling - Origin Vault has asked him about a revenue-share partnership. That proposal is on HIS deal, not ours.
talking_points.why: Worth knowing before anyone proposes terms near it.
talking_points.source_line: Origin Vault. has asked me if I'll do some sort of a revenue share partnership.

talking_points.point: His own read on why a site converts is conversion science, not design taste - Boomtown gets him ~10% visitor-to-lead where he says some sites run 5%. Any site we hand him is judged against that number.
talking_points.why: It sets the acceptance criterion before we build.
talking_points.source_line: the site is only as good as it converts

benefits_to_us.benefit: The leak is quantified in his own numbers, not ours: ~$1,500/day on PPC, ~2 sales per 100 leads, ~$1,100 customer acquisition cost, and 85% of revenue on the one channel he says Google is closing. That is the whole leaky-bucket argument stated by the buyer.
He named the gap we close and admitted he cannot close it himself. Attribution reporting for organic is a deliverable, not a favour, and it is the one he will feel every week.
benefits_to_us.source_line: I don't know how to present that to them

benefits_to_us.benefit: He is already sold on the thesis. The work is not convincing him AI matters; it is being the one who ships before his October window.
benefits_to_us.source_line: I just feel like we have in our grasp institutional grade software

benefits_to_us.benefit: The SEO teardown was run live on his own site before any paperwork, and the schema defect is unfixable inside his hard-coded CMS template. That template constraint is precisely what a site we build removes.

He is paying an Upwork team on milestones for the internal app and calls it his first dev adventure. Four products, one first-time dev relationship and a hard October date is a delivery-capacity problem we are built for.
benefits_to_us.source_line: Built via Upwork dev team (milestone-based payments); first dev project undertaken
